newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-GEC makes new play for Thomson stake.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-GEC makes new play for Thomson stake.

text.p: Britain's General Electric Co Plc (GEC), undaunted by the French government's rejection of its bid for defence-electonics group Thomson-CSF, said on Friday it was still pursuing its plan to create a "world leader in defence electronics".

The British defence-electronics company said in a statement it was talking with French companies Alcatel Alsthom and Lagardere Group, which are allowed to bid for the state's 58 percent stake in Thomson.

GEC said it had been encouraged by the French government to open talks with Alcatel and Lagardere and declared its interest in creating a world leader by merging its GEC-Marconi division with Thomson.

"Whilst GEC regrets the decision of the French government announced earlier today to reject GEC's candidature proposal for the privatisation of Thomson-CSF, it has received encouragement from the French government to enter into discussions with its existing partners in France...This process has already started," the company said.
"The continued consolidation of the defence industry in the U.S. increases the urgency for the currently fragmented industry in Europe to be re-organised into larger, more competitive businesses."

The failure of GEC's direct bid for Thomson came as no surprise. It was confirmed by a French finance ministry statement which said "..the sale to a foreign company of more than 50 percent of the share capital of Thomson-CSF goes against the interests of national security."
Analysts said the latest development still left the door open for a possible deal that could give GEC control of up to 50 percent of a privatised Thomson.
The fit between GEC and Thomson was described as good, with the two firms already involved in a joint venture over sonars.
"The obvious logic is for GEC to come into the deal and not have full control but at least 50 percent control. I do not see it settling for less," said one industry analyst.

He called Alcatel a more obvious partner for GEC because of its existing links through a joint missiles venture. But he thought GEC was unlikely to be interested in a deal offering just a token stake of 10-20 percent.
"At the end of the day GEC won't be interested unless it has joint financial control, if it can't have total control."
Early last month GEC announced it had signed a memorandum of understanding with Italy's engineering group Finmeccanica on collaboration between their defence divisions.
GEC's managing director George Simpson has sought to shake the British corporate giant from its strategic slumber since taking over from veteran chief Lord Weinstock last year.
GEC's shares closed down 2 1/2 pence at 383p.
